correctness.rationale: For a proper coloring each color other than the cell color occurs 0/1/2 times in its open neighborhood according to membership in its row and column palettes, hence odd iff the palettes differ. In m<n an n-coloring must make row palettes size n and column palettes size m, and ordinary n-colorability follows cyclically. For square case n colors fail; n+1 colors imply the multiplicity of each missing row-color equals that of its missing column-color, forcing equal incident palettes. The cyclic construction q=n+2 with row indices Zq\{0,1}, col indices Zq\{0,2}, color a+b has missing consecutive vs distance-two pairs, and these cannot coincide for q>=5. Fresh independent program verified n up to 24, but analytic proof handles all orders.
